about.title: Woodside Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside's winding rural roads carry a mix of local traffic, cyclists, and weekend visitors, and the town still records dozens of injury collisions each year on corridors like Woodside Road, Portola Road, La Honda Road, and Rt 84. Many of these crashes cluster on Saturday mornings and early afternoons, when road use in the area picks up. Whether your collision happened at a rural intersection or along a winding stretch near the hills, getting medical care and documenting the scene matters right away. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured drivers, passengers, cyclists, and pedestrians in Woodside with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. California gives injury victims a limited window to pursue a claim, and insurance companies often move fast to gather statements that can work against you. Reaching out early, before evidence disappears or memories fade, gives an attorney more to work with on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road agency — is involved. An attorney can help sort out which deadline applies to a Woodside collision before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can collect. An attorney can help make sure the insurer isn't assigning you more blame than the facts support.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, hoping you'll say something that limits their payout. You're not required to give one, and an attorney can speak for you instead.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Rt 84 near Woodside — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Try to photograph the scene, vehicle damage, and any visible road conditions if you're able. Then consider speaking with an independent attorney before giving any statement to an insurance company.

items.question: Do I have a case if the crash happened on Portola Road or another rural stretch?
items.answer: It depends on the specific facts — how the collision happened, who was involved, and what evidence exists. A free consultation with an independent attorney can help you understand whether pursuing a claim makes sense for your situation.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive connects you with an independent attorney at no cost, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
